vectors.description: Seed M04-001: five tg128 reps, the last one 23 s; the outlier is excluded, the value is the lower median of the kept rates.

Seed M04-002a: MAD is 0 and the 13 s rep is 23% low, under the 25% cut, so it is KEPT. The reference (pre-B7) reports flags []; B7 adds THERMAL_DRIFT because the last kept rep is more than 100 permille slower than the first.
Seed M04-002b: MAD is 0 and the 14 s rep is 29% low: excluded; the four equal reps give high confidence.
Seed M04-003: two deviant reps out of five exceed floor(n/5) = 1, so none is excluded and the result is UNSTABLE, confidence low (B7 also flags drift: the last rep is 22% slower than the first).
Seed M04-004: paired pp512 spans (prefill and whole); rep 5 is an outlier and its whole span is excluded with it; TTFT is the upper median of the four kept whole spans.
Seed M04-005: a warm start with a tight spread caps confidence at medium.
Seed M04-006: contention of 120 permille caps confidence at medium.
Seed M04-007: sustained, flat for 10 minutes: no onset, stability 1000, high.
Seed M04-008: sustained, onset at 450 s, ended at 510 s (a soft ceiling held): the plateau was not reached, stability 800, medium.
Nearest-rank p10 over the four kept rates (benchmark.md 13.4 R6).
Nearest-rank p90 over the same four kept rates.
B7: reps that slow at every step are THERMAL_DRIFT and capped at low, although each rep is inside the MAD band.
B7: a fast first rep that the outlier rule would exclude is put back under drift; the value is over all five reps.
One rep is never enough: kept < 2 is insufficient and reports no value.
Two reps agree: kept = 2, spread 0, low (kept >= 3 is needed for medium).
A virtual machine caps confidence at medium.
Stream timing caps confidence at medium.
A phase restarted after a yield caps confidence at medium.
Swap growth above 256 MiB (SWAPPED) caps confidence at low.
Five tight reps with contention 50 permille: high (the boundary is inclusive).
Five tight reps with contention 51 permille: medium.
Spread of exactly 50 permille is still high (n = 5, kept 5).
The MAD outlier bound: a rep exactly 4449 milli-MADs from the median is NOT an outlier.
pp2048 at depth 0: the rate is over 2048 tokens.
Four reps, one outlier: floor(4/5) = 0 exclusions are allowed, so the series is UNSTABLE and every rep is kept.
Eight reps, two outliers: floor(8/5) = 1 exclusion is allowed, so the series is UNSTABLE and every rep is kept.
The design example's 29 windows (T3): onset at 195 s, plateau 5033, stability 663 permille, high.
A hard thermal ceiling ends the sustained phase: windows are kept, the flag HARD_CEILING is added and confidence is capped at medium.
A sustained phase that started warm has confidence low whatever it shows.
A short sustained phase (under 300 s, not a plateau) is low.
One window only: no onset is possible; the plateau is that window.
Peak is taken only from windows starting in the first 120 s: a faster window later does not become the peak.
Onset needs three consecutive smoothed windows below 900 permille of the peak: two are not enough.
The design session's worked example (a synthetic 16 GB phone, T1..T3 and a heat test): the five answers, the projected results and both renderings, all from one document.
The same example projected for the FILE audience: results lack the battery level, screen state and SoC temperature (P8).
A partial run (charger removed during the second tier): finished tiers are derived and projected; the heat test was not run, so question 4 says so.
A tier whose numerics check fails is skipped by every derived answer (a fast but wrong backend must not win).
T3 fits but was not measured: question 1 is ESTIMATED from T2 through the origin (benchmark.md 12.4 Q1).
T3 does not fit in the usable memory: question 1 is CANNOT HOLD IT.
No heat test in the document: the throttle answer is absent and the role rests on no plateau.
A desktop with a fast T3 plateau is a STRONG PROVIDER (question 5, first matching row).
An iPhone is a requester that helps only while open, whatever its numbers (question 5, row 1).
A document with a derived member is not a bench document (P7, at any depth).
The L1 bench set has no pins (BLOCKED(D18)): a document that names it cannot be decoded.
A tier whose sha256 differs from the compiled-in pin (the catalogue cannot substitute a test model).
Checked arithmetic: kvBytesPerToken * nCtx overflows 64 bits; the projection fails (INCONSISTENT) instead of wrapping.
Energy is not measured in the lab (deferred, design B31): a non-null energy is invalid.
An unknown member is invalid at schemaMinor 0.
Quick plan on a phone: one tier that fits, no heat test; the whole event log and the document hash are pinned.
Standard plan on a phone (T1, T2 and the heat test): the sustained phase ends at a plateau.
Standard plan with the 8B tier opted in (T3 runs the depth test and becomes the sustain tier).
Preflight refuses to start on a HOT device (thermal code 3).
Preflight refuses a phone that is not on its charger for the standard plan.
Preflight refuses when battery saver is on.
Preflight refuses the standard plan without a live thermal source (NO_THERMAL_SIGNAL).
Preflight refuses a virtual machine (the plan is not ci).
Preflight refuses when a test model is missing.
Preflight refuses when not even the smallest tier fits.
Preflight refuses when the contention spin is 2500 permille over the device's best.
Preflight refuses while the daemon has a request in flight.
The charger is removed mid-run: ABORTING, then FINALIZING with the finished tests; the document records run.abort.
User Stop: the same path as a hard ceiling.
A standalone shell sent to the background aborts at the next check.
A memory-pressure signal aborts.
A battery temperature at the hard ceiling (44.5 C) aborts.
The thermal source disappears: three failed polls abort (PROBE_LOST).
A real request arrives during a tier (daemon): YIELDED, 30 s idle, COOLING, and the tier restarts; its confidence is capped.
The third yield finishes the run early with DEVICE_BUSY.
A hard thermal ceiling in the sustained phase ends the phase (the windows are kept, endReason THERMAL_HARD) and the run completes.
A soft ceiling held for 120 s ends the sustained phase (THERMAL_SOFT).
A device that never slows down reaches the time cap (TIME_CAP, no onset).
An engine that runs out of memory loading a tier is a typed failure: the tier is skipped and the run goes on.

vectors.description: Standard plan on a desktop (T2, T3, T4; the headline tier also runs pp2048).
The ci plan: one tier, three tests, no heat test.
The quick run plan is compiled-in data; a document records the SHA-256 of its JCS bytes.
The standard run plan is compiled-in data; a document records the SHA-256 of its JCS bytes.
The ci run plan is compiled-in data; a document records the SHA-256 of its JCS bytes.
The compiled-in defaults contain no L1 (Llama) pin; L1 is loaded only under a D18 ruling flag and then has no pins at all (BLOCKED(D18)); Q1 pins are PROPOSED until the owner confirms each sha256.
Consent: the confirmed hash matches the shown text and the token is used once, within 5 minutes.
Consent: a hash that is not the hash of the text shown mints nothing.
Consent: a token expires 5 minutes after minting.
Consent: a token is single-use.
Consent: a token covers exactly the plan whose sheet was shown.
Consent: a sheet that has been run today asks for an extra tick before the heat test.
The governor state machine: every allowed edge (benchmark.md 11.4 with B9); every other pair is refused by `Governor.to`.
Android: thermal status severe is a hard ceiling.
Android: headroom 950 permille is a soft ceiling.
Android: battery 44.0 C is a hard ceiling; 43.9 C only a soft one.
Android: a battery level under 200 permille is a hard ceiling.
iOS: no soft ceiling; thermal state serious is hard; Low Power Mode is hard.
macOS: serious is soft, critical is hard, a laptop losing AC is hard.
Linux: code 3 (at the passive trip) is soft, code 4 is hard.
Steam Deck: other processes' GPU load held for 10 s is a hard ceiling (a game started).
Nothing applies: no ceiling.
